title: Sioux City leaders and lawmakers presented with grim numbers concerning Iowa cancer rate - NewsBreak
text:
By Alex Prieto-Rivero ,
1 days ago
SIOUX CITY , Iowa ( KCAU ) — Local and city leaders gathered at the Aalfs Downtown Library to learn about environmental risk factors associated with rising cancer rates across Iowa.
“Our mission is to create a just and healthy environment for all Iowans,” said Iowa Environmental Council Water Program Director Colleen Fowle.
Since 2023, the state of Iowa has had the second-highest cancer rate in the United States. Iowa is also one of only three states where the cancer rate is increasing.
“Through our research and through our collaboration with our scientific advisory panel, they identified four key areas that we should hone in on for this research,” said Fowle. “Those four key areas are radon exposure in our homes and businesses, nitrate in our drinking water, pesticides through multiple exposure pathways, through air and water, and forever chemicals, also known as PFAS.”
Story continues below
City council members Rick Bertrand and Ike Rayford offered possible solutions.
“One particular thing that came to mind was lead,” said Rayford. “We know that at some point we are going to have to really take a look at our residents in homes that have lead issues and those things.”
“This is going to take some time,” said Bertrand. “But it starts with meetings like today. To educate ourselves and to understand there is solutions and a lot of this is manmade and timely.”
Iowa State Senator Catelin Drey said that efforts are being made in Des Moines to help lower the cancer rate.
“One of the things that we passed in the last legislative session was also funding for pediatric cancer research, which is one kind of step,” said Drey. “We are aware, now, that children are not just small adults. They have different needs and different factors that go into treating and addressing childhood cancer. But that level of dedication and research is going to be necessary at all levels as we move forward.”
